52988-the-white-wampum.title: The White Wampvm
52988-the-white-wampum.creator: E·Pavline Johnson
52988-the-white-wampum.description: A book by E·Pavline Johnson. Him who had flung their warriors into graves,  Him who had crushed them underneath his heel,  Whose arm was iron, and whose heart was steel  To all--save me, Ojistoh, chosen wife  Of my great Mohawk, white star of his life.

arxiv-2105-05845.creator: Jonathan Pila, Thomas Scanlon
arxiv-2105-05845.description: Abstract . We prove function field versions of the Zilber-Pink conjectures for varieties supporting a variation of Hodge structures. A form of these results for Shimura varieties in the context of unlikely intersections is the following. Let S S be a connected pure Shimura variety with a fixed quasiprojective embedding.

arxiv-2311-18763.title: Continual Diffusion with STAMINA: STack-And-Mask INcremental Adapters
arxiv-2311-18763.creator: James Seale Smith Yen-Chang Hsu Zsolt Kira Yilin Shen Hongxia Jin
arxiv-2311-18763.description: Abstract Recent work has demonstrated a remarkable ability to customize text-to-image diffusion models to multiple, fine-grained concepts in a sequential (i.e., continual) manner while only providing a few example images for each concept. This setting is known as continual diffusion . Here, we ask the question: Can we scale these methods to longer concept sequences without forgetting?

arxiv-2412-03316.title: First Detection of Radio Emission from the Intermediate Mass Black Hole in POX 52: Deep Multi-Band Observations with ATCA and VLA
arxiv-2412-03316.creator: Qi Yuan, Hengxiao Guo, Minfeng Gu, Jamie Stevens, Philip G. Edwards, Yongjun Chen, Wenwen Zuo, Jingbo Sun, Jun Yang, Paulina Lira, Tao An, Renzhi Su, Yuanqi Liu, Yijun Wang, Ning Chang, Pengfei Jiang, Ming Zhang
arxiv-2412-03316.description: Abstract We present the first multi-band centimeter detection of POX 52, a nearby dwarf galaxy believed to harbor a robust intermediate mass black hole (IMBH). pmc-11447231.title: Development and challenge of coal-based nanocarbon materials and their application in water treatment: a review
pmc-11447231.creator: MingShuai Xie, HongChao Luo, XinJuan Liu, ChaoChuang Yin
pmc-11447231.description: Under the dual pressures of environmental protection and energy security, the development and application of coal-based nanocarbon materials, supported by the technical concepts of molecular chemical engineering and nanomaterial science, is of significant importance for achieving the high-value clean utilization of coal. Furthermore, it serves as an effective means to assist in the realization of dual carbon goals.

pmc-12655992.title: ACI-GNN: Lightweight All-Channel Interaction Graph Neural Network for Multi-Sensor Coal-Rock Cutting Recognition
pmc-12655992.creator: Zhixin Jin, Jie Cheng, Wenyan Cao, Hongwei Wang, Jiaxin Zhang, Zeping Liu, Haoran Wang, Jianzhong Li, Marcin Woźniak
pmc-12655992.description: To address the current challenges of low single-sensor recognition accuracy for coal and rock cutting states, redundant channel feature responses, and poor performance in traditional neural network models, this paper proposes a new multi-sensor coal and rock cutting state recognition model based on a graph neural network (GNN).

pmc-13196399.title: A proof-of-concept study of an albumin-based bilayered scaffold for cartilage regeneration
pmc-13196399.creator: Christelle Bertsch, Florent Colin, Eya Aloui, Julien Graff, Maria Cristina Antal, Sabine Kuchler-Bopp, Adrien Moya, Romy Marek, Sven Zaugg, Eric Mathieu, Claire Thibault, Christian Debry, Jordan Beurton, Bernard Senger, Benoit Frisch, Michael de Wild, Arnaud Scherberich, Philippe Lavalle, Léa Fath
pmc-13196399.description: Cartilage, particularly hyaline cartilage, is essential for structural and functional integrity in otorhinolaryngological region (nose, ears, larynx, and trachea) but exhibits limited regenerative capacity due to its avascular nature. Current clinical strategies, including microfracture, autologous chondrocyte implantation, and cartilage grafting remain limited by poor integration, donor site morbidity, and fibrocartilage formation rather than hyaline cartilage.

pmc-13640173.title: Chelerythrine: a novel candidate for targeting miR-21/PTEN/PI3K/AKT in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
pmc-13640173.creator: Wenqing Zhang, Jie Liu, Huimei Chen, Lan He, Xianwen Wang, Yingchun He, Jingying Fan
pmc-13640173.description: BackgroundNasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is characterized by high metastatic potential and therapeutic resistance, necessitating the development of novel and safe therapeutic strategies. Hyperactivation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, often driven by the oncogenic microRNA-21 (miR-21) and the subsequent suppression of PTEN, plays a key role in NPC progression.
